---
title: "Bayesian Cox frailty model: basic run"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(rstan)
library(survival)
options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())
rstan_options(auto_write = TRUE)
```

## Data

The `kidney` dataset from `survival`. The Stan model assumes rows are sorted by ascending time.

```{r data}
k <- survival::kidney
k <- k[order(k$time), ]

# Covariates exactly as in the paper: age in years, sex coded 1 = male, 2 = female,
# 0/1 indicators for disease types GN, AN, PKD (Other is the baseline).
X <- cbind(age = k$age,
           sex = k$sex,
           GN  = as.integer(k$disease == "GN"),
           AN  = as.integer(k$disease == "AN"),
           PKD = as.integer(k$disease == "PKD"))

# Making an r matrix, it follows the convention for r as described in the paper
r <- matrix(0,
            byrow = T,
            ncol = 38,
            nrow = 76)
r[cbind(1:nrow(k), k$id)] <- 1
proper_r <- apply(r, 2, cumsum)
proper_r <- rbind(0, proper_r[-nrow(proper_r), ])
proper_r <- proper_r + 1 

# Finding where the occurrences happen for the patients in the dataset
dummy_for_a <- matrix(0, nrow = 38, ncol = 2)
for (i in 1:38) {
  dummy_for_a[i, ] <- which(k$id == i)
}

## Defining the data
stan_data <- list(N = nrow(k),
                  M = length(unique(k$id)),
                  P = ncol(X),
                  m = 2,
                  C = k$status,
                  pid = k$id,
                  X = X,
                  r = proper_r,
                  a_ind = dummy_for_a,
                  sigma = 0.5)
```

## Fit

```{r fit, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results="hide"}
fit <- stan("path",
            data = stan_data,
            seed = 1,
            chains = 4,
            iter = 5000,
            refresh = 0,
            verbose = T)
```

## Results

```{r summary}
print(fit, pars = c("beta", "sigma2"), probs = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))
```

Paper values for comparison (McGilchrist & Aisbett 1991, Table 2): age 0.0063, sex -1.7947, GN 0.2062, AN 0.4099, PKD -1.2961, sigma^2 0.3821.

```{r frailties}
print(fit, pars = "Z", probs = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))
```
